what_happened: The agent running Athena logged a mistake on 13 Nov (20261113-132803-knm6) and told Sri that a writer ran 90 minutes past an unenforced 616 s deadline. The steward later found (work item 20261114-022805-2xbq) that 616 s was the time left after a login-expiry retry on a 5400 s cap. The limit was not broken. The agent had read the deadline number in the stop reason at face value. It did not check the job's configured cap or its retry history. No job work was judged.
cause: The agent reports on shared state without resolving what it refers to, and Athena does not guard it. Here the state was what a deadline number in a stop reason means. Athena's stop reason shows only the remaining deadline (616 s). It does not show the configured cap or say that a retry used part of it. Nothing ties a claim of a broken limit to the job's cap and retry history. The only guard is the agent's own habit of checking the records first.
other_causes: The stop reason text gives a bare number with no label saying it is time left after a retry rather than the configured limit.
The mistake was logged and reported to the owner as fact, with no second check, before the steward looked at it.
open_hypotheses: Whether the same writer really ran 90 minutes in total. The fields do not say whether the overrun was real under the 5400 s cap or just a misreading of the numbers.
prevention: Make the deadline stop reason print the configured cap, the time used before and after each retry, and the time left, so a leftover number cannot be read as the limit. Add a check on the intervention-logging path. Before a claim that a stage broke its time limit is logged, the check compares the stage's recorded runtime with the configured cap and the retry history, and refuses the claim if the runtime is within the cap.
proposed_request: Change the stage-deadline stop reason so it records and prints three values: the configured cap for the stage, the time already used including any login-expiry or other retries, and the time left for this attempt. Add a check in the code that logs a mistake or intervention claiming a stage exceeded its deadline: it must compare the stage's actual runtime with the configured cap and the retry history from the job records, and refuse or flag the claim when the runtime is within the cap. Add tests for a run that retries after a login expiry on a 5400 s cap and ends with 616 s left, and show that it is not reported as a broken deadline. Add a CHANGELOG.md entry.
